text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Negotiations over a new premier are to continue today. Tiit Vaehi will not resign until after his visit to Ukraine, due February 20-22, the government press service said.

- The North Estonian town of Kohtla-Jarve protested it was left out of the privatisation process of the Kiviter Chemical plant and proposed to the Privatisation Agency to terminate talks with Infravest, a potential buyer of the plant.
- France is a firm ally of Estonia in its goal of EU membership, President Meri said on his return from Paris.
- Colonel Ants Laaneots has been reappointed the acting chief-of-staff of the Defence Forces. Laaneots held this post in 1991-1995 until he was dismissed by General Aleksander Einseln.
- A trial of 44 young criminals, 28 of them minors, involved in property crimes, began in Parnu.
- Two groups of Estonian mountain climbers reached the highest point in America in January, the 6,959-metre Aconcagua mountain.
- President Lennart Meri is still undecided on awarding the orders of merit that he is expected to present on the Independence Day on February 24.
